Project fork and source: [Pau-Rico/datascience_env_monit](https://github.com/Pau-Rico/datascience_env_monit).

# E1. Question and hypothesis

**Question.** For each tower, how do annual mean air temperature and annual
precipitation compare with its WorldClim 1970–2000 normal?

**Hypothesis.** I expect annual temperatures to be mostly above the
1970–2000 normal. I expect precipitation to vary between towers and years.
Recent warming may raise temperatures above the older normal. Precipitation
may change more from year to year and from site to site.

The five towers are in different regions and ecosystems. They are useful for
comparing sites, but they do not represent all climates. Their records cover
different periods, so the sites are not compared over the same years.

# E2. Data

The analysis uses FLUXNET daily data and two Block 5 datasets: WorldClim and
ERA5-Land.

| Dataset | Variables used | Spatial resolution | Time resolution and period | Download date | Script and changes | Citation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FLUXNET | `TA_F` (air temperature), `TA_F_QC` (temperature QC), `P_F` (precipitation), `P_F_QC` (precipitation QC) | Tower measurement, approximate flux footprint 100 m–1 km | Daily, 1999–2025. Site periods are in Table @tbl-sites | 20 Nov 2026 | Existing `FLUXMET_DD` files in `data/raw`. QC fields were read directly because `09_merge.py` omits them | Site data-product citations and acknowledgement in E6, Pastorello et al. (2020) |
| WorldClim 2.1 | BIO1 (temperature normal, °C), BIO12 (precipitation normal, mm) | 5 arc-minutes, approximately 9 km | 1970–2000 climate normals | 20 Nov 2026 | `scripts/block5/02_worldclim.py`, 5′ resolution and nearest-cell sampling | Fick & Hijmans (2017) |
| ERA5-Land | `t2m_C` (2 m air temperature) | 0.1°, approximately 9 km | Daily means derived from hourly data. Last available 8–10 tower years, listed in Table @tbl-sites | 20 and 25 Nov 2026 | `scripts/block5/01_era5land.py`, 10-year setting. No analysis settings changed | Muñoz-Sabater et al. (2021) |

ERA5-Land daily means use UTC days. The downloaded ERA5-Land files have no
precipitation values, so I use FLUXNET for precipitation.

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

from pathlib import Path
import re
import zipfile

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

PROJECT_ROOT = Path.cwd()
if not (PROJECT_ROOT / "data" / "raw").exists():
    PROJECT_ROOT = Path("..").resolve()

SITE_IDS = ["AU-TTE", "BE-Bra", "CH-Oe1", "JP-Ynf", "US-MN2"]
QC_THRESHOLD = 0.90
site_colors = dict(zip(SITE_IDS, plt.get_cmap("tab10").colors[:5]))

worldclim_path = (
    PROJECT_ROOT / "data" / "external" / "worldclim" / "worldclim_bio_my_sites.csv"
)
if not worldclim_path.exists():
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"WorldClim output not found: {worldclim_path}")
worldclim = pd.read_csv(worldclim_path)
worldclim = worldclim[["site_id", "BIO1", "BIO12"]].copy()

flux_parts = []
required_columns = {"TIMESTAMP", "TA_F", "TA_F_QC", "P_F", "P_F_QC"}
for zip_path in sorted((PROJECT_ROOT / "data" / "raw").glob("*FLUXNET*.zip")):
    site_match = re.match(r"^[A-Z]+_([A-Z]{2}-[A-Za-z0-9]{3})_", zip_path.name)
    if not site_match or site_match.group(1) not in SITE_IDS:
        continue
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as archive:
        daily_members = [
            member for member in archive.namelist() if "FLUXMET_DD" in member
        ]
        if not daily_members:
            continue
        with archive.open(daily_members[0]) as daily_file:
            flux = pd.read_csv(
                daily_file,
                na_values=[-9999],
                usecols=lambda column: column in required_columns,
                dtype={"TIMESTAMP": str},
            )
    flux["date"] = pd.to_datetime(flux.pop("TIMESTAMP"), format="%Y%m%d")
    flux["site_id"] = site_match.group(1)
    flux_parts.append(flux)

if not flux_parts:
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        "No matching FLUXMET_DD daily files found in data/raw."
    )
flux_daily = pd.concat(flux_parts, ignore_index=True)
flux_daily["year"] = flux_daily["date"].dt.year

annual_flux = (
    flux_daily.groupby(["site_id", "year"], as_index=False)
    .agg(
        n_days=("date", "nunique"),
        n_ta=("TA_F", "count"),
        ta_mean_C=("TA_F", "mean"),
        ta_qc_fraction=("TA_F_QC", "mean"),
        n_precip=("P_F", "count"),
        precip_sum_mm=("P_F", "sum"),
        precip_qc_fraction=("P_F_QC", "mean"),
    )
)
annual_flux["ta_missing_days"] = annual_flux["n_days"] - annual_flux["n_ta"]
annual_flux["precip_missing_days"] = annual_flux["n_days"] - annual_flux["n_precip"]
annual = annual_flux.merge(worldclim, on="site_id", how="left", validate="many_to_one")
annual["temp_anomaly_C"] = annual["ta_mean_C"] - annual["BIO1"]
annual["precip_anomaly_mm"] = annual["precip_sum_mm"] - annual["BIO12"]

era_daily_parts = []
era_dir = PROJECT_ROOT / "data" / "external" / "era5land"
for site_id in SITE_IDS:
    era_path = era_dir / f"{site_id}_era5land_daily.csv"
    if not era_path.exists():
        continue
    era_daily = pd.read_csv(era_path, parse_dates=["date"])
    if "t2m_C" not in era_daily.columns:
        raise ValueError(f"Expected t2m_C in {era_path}")
    era_daily = era_daily[["date", "site_id", "t2m_C"]].copy()
    era_daily["year"] = era_daily["date"].dt.year
    era_years = (
        era_daily.groupby(["site_id", "year"], as_index=False)
        .agg(
            era5_days=("t2m_C", "count"),
            era5_mean_C=("t2m_C", "mean"),
        )
    )
    era_daily_parts.append(era_years)

if era_daily_parts:
    era_annual = pd.concat(era_daily_parts, ignore_index=True)
else:
    era_annual = pd.DataFrame(
        columns=["site_id", "year", "era5_days", "era5_mean_C"]
    )

annual = annual.merge(
    era_annual, on=["site_id", "year"], how="left", validate="one_to_one"
)
annual["era5_anomaly_C"] = annual["era5_mean_C"] - annual["BIO1"]
```

Table @tbl-sites describes the two gridded datasets at each tower and the
available FLUXNET record. A blank ERA5-Land period means that the file had no
valid daily 2 m temperature values for that tower.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-sites
#| tbl-cap: "WorldClim normals and data coverage at the five selected towers."

coverage = (
    annual.groupby("site_id", as_index=False)
    .agg(
        flux_first_year=("year", "min"),
        flux_last_year=("year", "max"),
        flux_years=("year", "nunique"),
        flux_days=("n_days", "sum"),
        ta_missing_days=("ta_missing_days", "sum"),
        precip_missing_days=("precip_missing_days", "sum"),
        mean_TA_QC=("ta_qc_fraction", "mean"),
        mean_P_QC=("precip_qc_fraction", "mean"),
    )
)

valid_era = annual.dropna(subset=["era5_anomaly_C"])
era_coverage = (
    valid_era.groupby("site_id", as_index=False)
    .agg(
        era5_first_year=("year", "min"),
        era5_last_year=("year", "max"),
        era5_years=("year", "nunique"),
        era5_valid_days=("era5_days", "sum"),
        mean_era5_temp_C=("era5_mean_C", "mean"),
        mean_era5_departure_C=("era5_anomaly_C", "mean"),
    )
)
site_summary = (
    worldclim.merge(coverage, on="site_id", how="left", validate="one_to_one")
    .merge(era_coverage, on="site_id", how="left", validate="one_to_one")
)
site_summary["era5_years"] = site_summary["era5_years"].fillna(0).astype(int)
site_summary["era5_valid_days"] = site_summary["era5_valid_days"].fillna(0).astype(int)

site_summary[
    [
        "site_id",
        "BIO1",
        "BIO12",
        "flux_first_year",
        "flux_last_year",
        "flux_years",
        "flux_days",
        "ta_missing_days",
        "precip_missing_days",
        "mean_TA_QC",
        "mean_P_QC",
        "era5_first_year",
        "era5_last_year",
        "era5_years",
        "era5_valid_days",
        "mean_era5_temp_C",
        "mean_era5_departure_C",
    ]
].round(2)
```

Each tower has its own WorldClim normals. The WorldClim file contains all five
towers. ERA5-Land has complete daily data for its available periods at
AU-TTE, BE-Bra, CH-Oe1, and US-MN2. The JP-Ynf file has 3,652 dates, but all
`t2m_C` values are missing. I leave them missing and do not fill them from
another dataset or tower.

# E3. Methods

**Download and extraction.** WorldClim BIO1 and BIO12 were sampled from the
nearest 5′ grid cells using the tower coordinates in EPSG:4326. ERA5-Land
daily data were requested from the nearest 0.1° grid cell for the last 10
available years, using coordinates rounded to three decimal places. The
analysis settings were unchanged, and the only local script edit replaced the
example CDS-key text with a placeholder.

**Flux preparation and quality control.** I read the daily `FLUXMET_DD` files
from the five original ZIP files and treated `-9999` as missing. Annual air
temperature is the mean of daily `TA_F` (°C). Annual precipitation is the sum
of daily `P_F` (mm). For each year, I calculated the mean daily
`TA_F_QC` and `P_F_QC` values. The merge script does not include these QC
columns, so I read them from the original daily files. The data contain
25,202 tower-days and 69 complete site-years. There are no missing `TA_F` or
`P_F` values.

The first calculation uses all years, regardless of QC. The second keeps
years with a mean annual QC fraction of at least 0.90. This cutoff is my
choice, not an official FLUXNET pass/fail rule. QC fractions describe the
quality of gap-filled data. A year that passes the cutoff can still include
gap-filled data. I apply the cutoff separately to temperature and
precipitation.

**Alignment and analysis.** I joined annual FLUXNET values to the WorldClim
BIO1 and BIO12 values for each tower, using `site_id` and year. Temperature
departure is `annual mean TA_F − BIO1`. Precipitation departure is
`annual sum P_F − BIO12`. Positive values mean warmer or wetter conditions
than that tower's normal. I averaged ERA5-Land daily `t2m_C` by calendar year
(UTC) and compared it with BIO1. Missing values stayed as `NA`.

The pooled median gives each site-year equal weight. Towers with longer
records therefore have more influence. Annual values from one tower may not
be independent of each other.

# E4. Results

The temperature figure compares annual FLUXNET and ERA5-Land departures from
each tower's WorldClim normal. The precipitation figure shows FLUXNET
departures from WorldClim BIO12. The zero line means the value equals the
WorldClim normal. FLUXNET years below the 0.90 QC cutoff are shown with
transparent points and dashed lines. All years remain visible.

```{python}
#| label: temperature-figure
#| fig-cap: "Annual mean air-temperature departure from each tower's WorldClim BIO1 normal. Circles are FLUXNET annual values and diamonds are ERA5-Land annual values. The zero line indicates the site-specific normal. FLUXNET years with annual QC below 0.90 are semi-transparent and dashed. ERA5-Land is unavailable for JP-Ynf."

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(14, 8), sharey=True, constrained_layout=True)
for ax, site_id in zip(axes.flat, SITE_IDS):
    site = annual[annual["site_id"] == site_id].sort_values("year")
    for i in range(len(site) - 1):
        first = site.iloc[i]
        second = site.iloc[i + 1]
        low_qc = (
            first["ta_qc_fraction"] < QC_THRESHOLD
            or second["ta_qc_fraction"] < QC_THRESHOLD
        )
        ax.plot(
            [first["year"], second["year"]],
            [first["temp_anomaly_C"], second["temp_anomaly_C"]],
            color=site_colors[site_id],
            linewidth=1.35,
            linestyle="--" if low_qc else "-",
            alpha=0.5 if low_qc else 1,
            zorder=2,
        )
    good = site[site["ta_qc_fraction"] >= QC_THRESHOLD]
    low = site[site["ta_qc_fraction"] < QC_THRESHOLD]
    ax.scatter(
        good["year"], good["temp_anomaly_C"], color=site_colors[site_id],
        edgecolor=site_colors[site_id], s=38, zorder=4
    )
    ax.scatter(
        low["year"], low["temp_anomaly_C"], color=site_colors[site_id],
        edgecolor=site_colors[site_id], alpha=0.5, s=38, zorder=4
    )
    era = site.dropna(subset=["era5_anomaly_C"])
    if not era.empty:
        ax.plot(
            era["year"], era["era5_anomaly_C"], color="0.25",
            linestyle=":", linewidth=1.4, marker="D", markersize=4.5, zorder=3
        )
    else:
        ax.text(
            0.5, 0.53, "ERA5-Land unavailable", transform=ax.transAxes,
            ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9
        )
    ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.9, linestyle="--", zorder=1)
    ax.set_title(site_id)
    ax.set_xlabel("Year")
    ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)

legend_ax = axes.flat[5]
legend_ax.axis("off")
legend_ax.legend(
    handles=[
        Line2D([0], [0], color="0.25", marker="o", linestyle="-",
               label="FLUXNET, QC ≥ 0.90"),
        Line2D([0], [0], color="0.25", marker="o", linestyle="--", alpha=0.5,
               label="FLUXNET, QC < 0.90"),
        Line2D([0], [0], color="0.25", marker="D", linestyle=":",
               label="ERA5-Land"),
    ],
    loc="center",
    title="Annual temperature departure",
)
fig.supylabel("Difference from WorldClim mean annual temperature (°C)")
fig.suptitle("Annual air-temperature difference from WorldClim normal", fontsize=15)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: precipitation-figure
#| fig-cap: "Annual FLUXNET precipitation departure from each tower's WorldClim BIO12 normal. The zero line indicates the site-specific normal. Years with annual P_F_QC below 0.90 are semi-transparent and connected with dashed segments. JP-Ynf precipitation values are shown but have P_F_QC = 0 in every year."

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(14, 8), sharey=True, constrained_layout=True)
for ax, site_id in zip(axes.flat, SITE_IDS):
    site = annual[annual["site_id"] == site_id].sort_values("year")
    for i in range(len(site) - 1):
        first = site.iloc[i]
        second = site.iloc[i + 1]
        low_qc = (
            first["precip_qc_fraction"] < QC_THRESHOLD
            or second["precip_qc_fraction"] < QC_THRESHOLD
        )
        ax.plot(
            [first["year"], second["year"]],
            [first["precip_anomaly_mm"], second["precip_anomaly_mm"]],
            color=site_colors[site_id],
            linewidth=1.35,
            linestyle="--" if low_qc else "-",
            alpha=0.5 if low_qc else 1,
            zorder=2,
        )
    good = site[site["precip_qc_fraction"] >= QC_THRESHOLD]
    low = site[site["precip_qc_fraction"] < QC_THRESHOLD]
    ax.scatter(
        good["year"], good["precip_anomaly_mm"], color=site_colors[site_id],
        edgecolor=site_colors[site_id], s=38, zorder=4
    )
    ax.scatter(
        low["year"], low["precip_anomaly_mm"], color=site_colors[site_id],
        edgecolor=site_colors[site_id], alpha=0.5, s=38, zorder=4
    )
    ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.9, linestyle="--", zorder=1)
    ax.set_title(site_id)
    ax.set_xlabel("Year")
    ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)

axes.flat[5].axis("off")
fig.supylabel("Difference from WorldClim annual precipitation (mm/year)")
fig.suptitle("Annual precipitation difference from WorldClim normal", fontsize=15)
plt.show()
```

The table shows medians and means of annual departures. It includes all years
and a second calculation with annual QC ≥ 0.90.

```{python}
#| label: anomaly-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Annual climate departures from WorldClim, with unfiltered and QC ≥ 0.90 summaries."

summary_rows = []
for variable, value_col, qc_col in [
    ("Temperature (°C)", "temp_anomaly_C", "ta_qc_fraction"),
    ("Precipitation (mm/year)", "precip_anomaly_mm", "precip_qc_fraction"),
]:
    for label, subset in [
        ("No QC filter", annual),
        ("Annual QC ≥ 0.90", annual[annual[qc_col] >= QC_THRESHOLD]),
    ]:
        valid = subset.dropna(subset=[value_col])
        summary_rows.append(
            {
                "Variable": variable,
                "Version": label,
                "Site-years (n)": len(valid),
                "Towers (n)": valid["site_id"].nunique(),
                "Pooled mean": valid[value_col].mean(),
                "Pooled median": valid[value_col].median(),
            }
        )
summary_table = pd.DataFrame(summary_rows)
summary_table.round(2)
```

Without QC filtering, the median departure is **+0.50 °C** for temperature
(69 site-years, five towers) and **+34.91 mm/year** for precipitation
(69 site-years, five towers). With annual QC ≥ 0.90, the medians are
**+0.64 °C** (54 site-years, five towers) and **−8.93 mm/year**
(47 site-years, four towers). These results describe the available site-years.
They are not estimates of a global climate trend.

The unfiltered means are **+0.48 °C** and **+736.65 mm/year**. The high
precipitation mean is mainly caused by the unreliable JP-Ynf precipitation
data. At JP-Ynf, `P_F_QC` is zero in all ten years, so no years from this site
pass the precipitation QC cutoff. I include the unfiltered result for
comparison, but it should not be treated as reliable.

As a second temperature check, the median of the four tower means for
ERA5-Land is **+1.04 °C** (38 site-years). JP-Ynf has no valid ERA5-Land data.
The other four tower means are above their WorldClim normals. ERA5-Land does
not provide precipitation data for this analysis.

# E5. Discussion

The temperature results support the hypothesis at most towers. The
QC-filtered median is above the WorldClim normal, and all four towers with
ERA5-Land data also have positive mean departures. Not every year is warmer
than normal. Most annual temperature departures at JP-Ynf are below its
normal. Precipitation departures differ among towers and years. The unfiltered
result is affected by JP-Ynf, where precipitation QC is zero. WorldClim and
ERA5-Land grid cells are about 9 km wide. This is much larger than the
approximate 100 m–1 km tower footprint, so grid values may not match the
conditions near a tower. WorldClim describes 1970–2000, while tower records
cover different years from 1999 to 2025. These results show differences from
an older normal, not a trend based on the same years. The main limits are
missing ERA5-Land temperature for JP-Ynf, poor precipitation QC there, the
chosen 0.90 cutoff, and the small number of towers. Values from different
years at one tower may not be independent.
